diagnoses.description:
The fix targeted idempotency/session creation but introduced cross-test/session-lifecycle side effects: because Client is a singleton, starting a session implicitly (or leaving one active) causes later explicit agentops.start_session() calls in tests to no-op with “session already started”, altering expected network calls and tag handling.
Evidence: The patch adds logic in init() to mutate the singleton client config and auto-start sessions based on existing session state (Turn 57 patch shows new block; Turn 60 shows it present in agentops/__init__.py).
Trajectory location: turn 50-58 (patch_3.diff content and applied change)

Session state is being retained across tests and/or started earlier than the tests intend; start_session() refuses to start a new session and therefore does not perform the mocked HTTP request(s) the tests assert on. The patch changed session-init semantics without resetting singleton state between tests.
Evidence: Pytest now reports 5 failures, and every failing test’s log includes “WARNING agentops:client.py:245 🖇 AgentOps: Cannot start session - session already started”. Tests expecting 1 session-start request see 0 (tests/test_session.py::test_session), and decorator tests expecting an extra event/end request see fewer requests than expected.
Trajectory location: turn 59 (test regressions after patch_3 applied)

The patch was authored against a repository file that already contains redacted placeholders; propagating these placeholders risks producing syntactically invalid Python or incorrect runtime behavior depending on how the redactions are represented in the actual file. Even if the environment tolerates it here, it is not a robust fix and complicates correct configuration handling.
Evidence: The diff/code contains placeholder tokens like “api_key: ***REDACTED***” and assignments “c.config.api_key = ***REDACTED***” (Turn 57 and Turn 60).
Trajectory location: turn 50-60 (patch_3.diff and resulting code)

Incorrect unified diff hunk headers/line counts and/or missing required context lines initially produced invalid patch format, slowing iteration and increasing risk of incorrect modifications.
Evidence: git apply failed twice: “error: corrupt patch at line 39” (Turn 51) and “error: corrupt patch at line 30” (Turn 55) before being corrected.
Trajectory location: turn 51 and turn 55 (failed patch application attempts)
